lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my child Alex. He's 18 years old and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, eligibility depends on whether he is in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Studying for A-levels at sixth form college would typically count as approved education.

Now I need to ask about your relationship to Alex and your living situation:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, are you paying at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep** (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me at the moment. But I do help out financially - I contribute towards his upkeep, you know, helping with clothes, travel costs, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To determine if your contributions are sufficient for Child Benefit eligibility, I need to understand the amount you're contributing.

**Are you contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards Alex's upkeep?** 

For reference, the current Child Benefit rate for one child is £25.60 per week (or about £111 per month). Your contributions can include things like clothes, travel costs, food, pocket money, and other support for his upkeep.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute about £30 a week towards his costs, so that should be enough.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's very helpful.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your own circumstances:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to check a few more things about Alex's situation:

**Is Alex working at all, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, the person he lives with, or another parent/guardian?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits himself.

**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ **Age and education**: Alex is 18 and studying for A-levels at sixth form college, which counts as approved education. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training.

✓ **Responsibility for the child**: Although Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing approximately £30 per week towards his upkeep (clothes, travel costs, etc.), which is more than the Child Benefit rate. This establishes that you're responsible for him under the rules.

✓ **Other requirements met**: 
- You live in the UK
- Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
- Alex is not receiving benefits in his own right
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**Important note**: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay a High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might need to pay some or all of it back through your tax return.

If you'd like to proceed with claiming, you can apply for Child Benefit through HMRC. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
